title: Wall-clock timing assertions baked into functional specs
evidence: tests/acceptance/test_brazilian_soccer_questions.py:176-183 call confirm_answered_within(seconds=5) and seconds=2; mcp_driver.py:81 does a hard pass/fail on elapsed wall-clock time
suggestion: Move latency SLOs to a separate performance check (or monitoring); under CPU/RAM contention these thresholds flake and compromise the suite's releasability signal

title: Assertions pinned to brittle magic numbers from real third-party data
evidence: tests/acceptance/test_brazilian_soccer_questions.py:17,27,44 confirm_match_count(38); :62 confirm_record(matches=19); :85 confirm_champion('Flamengo', points=90) — all derived from Kaggle CSV merge/dedup logic per docs/atdd-findings.md
suggestion: Separate behaviour tests (against a small synthetic dataset the DSL seeds) from a few real-data shape/relationship smoke checks; avoids red for data changes unrelated to behaviour

title: Non-standard MCP SDK API and loosely pinned dependency
evidence: server.py:8 imports MCPServer from mcp.server.mcpserver; mcp_driver.py:11 imports Client from top-level mcp; requirements.txt pins 'mcp>=2' (official SDK uses FastMCP and is 1.x)
suggestion: Pin the exact mcp package/version used so the stack is reproducible; the chosen API is not the mainstream modelcontextprotocol SDK surface

title: Query coverage exceeds the spec
evidence: server.py registers ~19 tools incl. derbies, club_profile, compare_seasons, libertadores_bracket, best_record, biggest_wins beyond the 12 pinned requirements
